claims.text: Large language models have significantly propelled the field of automatic text summarization.
Existing hallucination detection and mitigation methods often lack transparency in their underlying mechanisms.
The Question-Answer Generation, Sorting, and Evaluation (Q-S-E) methodology enables the quantitative detection of hallucinations in summaries.
An iterative hallucination resolution mechanism enhances the transparency of the summary modification process.
The proposed Q-S-E framework markedly improves the factual consistency of generated summaries.
The proposed Q-S-E framework preserves the informational completeness of summaries.

evidence.description: The framework employs a Question-Answer Generation, Sorting, and Evaluation (Q-S-E) methodology to enable quantitative detection of hallucinations in summaries.
Experimental results on three benchmark datasets (CNN/Daily Mail, PubMed, and ArXiv) demonstrate that the approach markedly improves the factual consistency of summaries.
Experimental results on three benchmark datasets (CNN/Daily Mail, PubMed, and ArXiv) demonstrate that the approach preserves the informational completeness of summaries.

methodologies.name: Q-S-E Hallucination Detection and Mitigation Framework
methodologies.description: A framework employing Question-Answer Generation, Sorting, and Evaluation alongside an iterative resolution mechanism to detect and mitigate hallucinations in text summarization.

limitations.text: Existing methods exhibit limitations in effectively detecting and mitigating hallucinations, often lacking transparency in their underlying mechanisms.
